v1.5 -- at L10, on 1.0.0_SA_CTO's ROUND-1 ANALYSIS (org/tier1_exec/1.0.0_SA_CTO/deliverables/ROUND_ANALYSIS_LGIC_NAMING_ROUND1_20260914.md), ruling the four slots round 1 measured as unruled (carrier C-S5) and two FWD-5 gaps (C-S8): resource.function (FN1), resource.qualifier (FN2, FN3), secret.purpose and iam_policy.purpose_slot (FN4), key.partition's {entity} (P1), key.scope_rule (SC1), system.vendor_through_tiers (SY1), grade.placeholder (PH1) and aws_fixed (AW1). v1.7 -- at L10, on 1.0.0_SA_CTO's ROUND-2 ANALYSIS (org/tier1_exec/1.0.0_SA_CTO/deliverables/ROUND_ANALYSIS_LGIC_NAMING_ROUND2_20260915.md): resource.function -- a noun-phrase function drops every token already written in the system or scope slot (FN1b, row C-S14), and only the resource's OWN kind is barred from its function (FN1c, row W4-S2); both bind the grade as well as the namer, while FN1's word-choice clauses bind the namer only. firm_forms.demo cites the registry row that defines it (RULING DM, row W6-S4). rows_owner: the registry now exists and governs where it and the seed differ. system.vendor_through_tiers' worked example is a name outside every naming-exercise item set (RULING EX1, row S15). The five ruled key segments, the grade signature and its verdicts are unchanged.

key.ruled: Andrew-direct 2026-09-13 ~03:2xZ card 1, verbatim; the five segments and their order are the ruling
key.container: {bucket} -- the bucket that holds the key; NEVER a segment of the key
key.leaf: {object} -- the file under {partition}; not part of the ruled string
key.source: a registry VENDOR key (a feed) or, for derived tiers, a PRODUCT or SYSTEM key
key.scope_rule: a vendor MASTER keeps its own scope (doctrine R3: two masters of one firm are two scopes, never commingled -- schwab/08242234/, never schwab/49financial/). For every other key the scope is its AUDIENCE: a FIRM when the data is one firm's; global when every firm shares it. A PRODUCT key is a scope only beneath a VENDOR source (a feed for the product: pathfinder/etfs), never beneath itself as the source -- mdpf/global/..., never mdpf/mdpf/... (SC1, v1.5; the master case written at v1.6)
key.table_case: snake_case; a NEW platinum leaf is a kebab-case .json file (the served names); see legacy_served_path
key.legacy_served_path: below {source}/{scope}/platinum/, a LEGACY served path keeps its bytes -- the table, a bare entity-id segment in the partition slot, and the file name -- because the frozen portal requests it by path; the kebab-case and hive forms bind NEW served families only (LGIC_NAMING v1.3, rows S6 and S8). MEMBERSHIP is data, never a name's shape: a path is legacy only if legacy_served_paths lists it (LGIC_NAMING v1.4, row S10)

legacy_served_paths.producer: LGIC_NAMING cell LN-g-1: every served path below {source}/{scope}/platinum/ that the frozen portal requests, with the portal vintage it read and the denominator printed. A CLOSED list: a frozen portal adds no request.
legacy_served_paths.until_present: grade() RAISES on a platinum key whose verdict turns on legacy membership -- a defect in this file, fixed here (grade.unplaceable), never guessed CONFORMANT or OUT-OF-PATTERN

key.code: tier code is a pipeline's code home (R16), beside its data: {source}/{scope}/code/{built_tier}/{file} -- the table slot carries the tier the code builds (bronze, silver or gold) and the file or bundle is a named leaf; Lambda deployment artifacts take the same form (R16 does not reach them; R1 grades their key). Legacy root code/ homes stay until their pipelines move (LGIC_NAMING v1.3, row S7; the canon's carve-out narrowed as LGIC_CANON-S1). A legacy root code/ key grades OUT-OF-PATTERN, its canonical_form the code-tier key; a verdict is not a mandate to move, so MDPF_CANON's frozen rollback objects keep that verdict and stay (LGIC_NAMING v1.4, row S10)
partition: {entity}={id} -- an entity partition; {entity} is the KEY COLUMN's name as the table carries it (advisor_id=A123), as date is the column in date=YYYY-MM-DD; the file is the object under it (doctrine R2; P1, v1.5)

resource.scope_when_shared: OMITTED -- a shared resource carries no scope token, never a placeholder
resource.function: names what the resource does. Where the item DESCRIBES the action with a verb, the function is that verb in its base form (publish, fetch, read, build, download); an agent noun describing the resource ITSELF is written as its verb (publisher -> publish, exporter -> export, scanner -> scan), because the kind names the thing. Where the item NAMES the process or subject as a noun phrase (the SmartX platform export, the Orion ingest, the price-refresh queue, pipeline alerts, delivery status), the function is that phrase as named, kebab-case, ONE token (as silver-chain), LESS every token already written in the system or scope slot: Inflection's Orion ingest is orion-inf-ingest, never orion-inf-orion-ingest; a subtraction that leaves no function token RAISES (grade.unplaceable) (FN1b, v1.7). The resource's OWN kind (kind.by_type for its type) is never written in its function; another type's kind that names the subject the resource serves is part of that phrase and stays (mdpf-gold-lambda-role is the role the gold lambda assumes) (FN1c, v1.7). FN1b and FN1c bind the GRADE as well as the namer, because both are read from the name alone; the word-choice clauses before them bind the NAMER, who has the item's description, and a grade keeps a function's words as written (FN1, v1.5; v1.7)
resource.qualifier: optional narrowing, written after the function: the TIER (bronze, silver, gold, platinum) or the named TABLE the action acts on, when the item names one -- any other object (figures, files, data, session data) is not written (FN2); a leg; or an environment (dev | prod). A CW_ALARM's qualifier is its condition noun (failure, error, latency), always written (FN3, v1.5)

kind.closed_at_l4: By subtraction from the live plane's 33 node types: ECS_TASK_DEFINITION, STATE_MACHINE, LOAD_BALANCER and ECS_CLUSTER had no kind in the brief's list -- added as task, sfn, lb and cluster (the last two each have one live node, opal-gateway and opal-globgrph, and are resources this estate mints). secret was DROPPED: secrets keep their own slash-path grammar, where a kind suffix would repeat the type. The brief's measured suffixes trigger, publisher, scanner are FUNCTION tokens, not kinds; their canonical spellings are the verbs trigger, publish and scan (FN1, v1.5).

types_not_graded_by_kind.EVENT_RULE: resource grammar with a CADENCE as the last slot (resource.last_slot)
types_not_graded_by_kind.SCHEDULE: resource grammar with a CADENCE as the last slot (resource.last_slot)
types_not_graded_by_kind.LOG_GROUP: derived: /aws/{service}/{resource-name}; conforms when its resource does (log_group)
types_not_graded_by_kind.S3_BUCKET_POLICY: carries its bucket's name exactly (15 of 15 live nodes); graded as that bucket
types_not_graded_by_kind.IAM_USER: NOT GRADED: named by its holder or issuer -- a person, the account root, an external identity provider named by its issuer URL (4 live nodes). The one machine user among them (github-actions-portal) is recorded, not graded; a remediation that converts it to a role takes the role grammar
types_not_graded_by_kind.ROUTE53_RECORD: NOT GRADED: a DNS record name (not_covered)
types_not_graded_by_kind.API_ROUTE: NOT GRADED: a served route contract (not_covered; infra/logic/07_ROUTING_REDERIVATION.md)
types_not_graded_by_kind.EVENT_SOURCE: NOT GRADED: an event-source expression or service name, a different grammar (not_covered)

secret.purpose: the credential's kind (credentials, token, key, password, certificate), preceded by the interface it opens when the item names one: api-credentials (FN4, v1.5)

iam_policy.purpose_slot: function -- FN1 and FN2 apply, written as one compound token (read-gold) (FN4, v1.5)

firm_forms.note: one token; the long and short forms are the same string. The identity registry defines it: infra/logic/registry/scopes.json row demo reads class FIRM, tenancy FIRM, tenant kind demo, so in every naming slot demo reads as a firm (RULING DM, row W6-S4, v1.7)

refused_tokens.bd: refused in EVERY slot (Andrew ~03:5xZ card 2). The vendor is blackdiamond; the firm is 49financial.
refused_tokens.mockadv: an alias only, recorded in the registry's alias rows as history; never minted

system.vendor_as_system_only_when: the resource IS the vendor integration
system.vendor_through_tiers: a resource that builds a firm's data from ONE vendor's feed IS that vendor's integration at every tier it builds (blackdiamond-cot-build-silver-profile); a resource that combines feeds takes the PRODUCT or PLATFORM_SUBSYSTEM that owns the combination (SY1, v1.5). A worked example here is kept outside every naming-exercise item set, so a briefing that carries this file never spells an item's answer (RULING EX1, row S15, v1.7)

reserved.opal: account-level platform resources only; never a null prefix before a real system

grade.signature: (name, type) -> (verdict, canonical_form); type is a node_type value (node_type_vocabulary)
grade.ALIAS: the grammar holds but a slot carries a registry alias spelling (for example inflection or bd in a resource name's scope slot); canonical_form is printed
grade.OUT-OF-PATTERN: the grammar fails (order, separator, case, a missing or unknown kind, a firm in the system slot); canonical_form is printed
grade.not_graded: a type marked NOT GRADED in types_not_graded_by_kind returns no verdict and is outside the grade's domain -- it is excluded, not a fourth verdict
grade.placeholder: a canonical_form may carry {system}, {source}, {scope} or {cadence} ONLY for a slot the name does not carry. Each is a typed gap, never a guess, filled from its source: {system} from the identity registry's resource-to-system rows (LGIC_ENFORCE), {source}/{scope} from the bucket, {cadence} from the schedule. The verdict stays exact, and the signature stays (name, type). FWD-5's correct name is complete for a name only when no placeholder remains (PH1, v1.5)
grade.unplaceable: RAISES. A name the tokeniser cannot place, a node_type absent from this file, or a token no registry row resolves, is a defect in the tokeniser, this file or the registry and is fixed there -- it is never filed under one of the three verdicts, and there is no fourth

not_covered: Terraform resource labels and module names (the executable layer's authoring surface; measured before its flagger is specified)
AWS-issued identifiers (KMS key ids, CloudFront distribution ids, service principals, VPC endpoint ids)
API route grammar (a served contract; infra/logic/07_ROUTING_REDERIVATION.md)

aws_fixed.rule: names AWS fixes are OUTSIDE the grade's domain, like the NOT GRADED types: excluded, never a fourth verdict. Extended when a new AWS-fixed name is measured (AW1, v1.5)
aws_fixed.by_arn: an IAM_POLICY whose ARN's account field is aws (arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/...) is AWS-managed -- read from the node's ARN, never from the name (ReadOnlyAccess carries no prefix)
aws_fixed.measured: row LGIC_NAMING-W1-S4 over LIVE_NAMES.json (vintage 2026-09-14 12:13:53 UTC): SECURITY_GROUP 1 of 26; IAM_POLICY 9 of 417 by prefix, plus ReadOnlyAccess; LOG_GROUP 4 of 264

renames_authorized: NONE. This schema grades; it moves no live name. Each remediation is minted where the resource lives, cites a row of the tension ranking, and carries its own sign-off.
